### A-ASM-01: In-game assessment is transparent and separated

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: ai_assessment, assessment · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** When gameplay is used to assess learning (stealth assessment), learners, teachers and guardians are told, assessment data is separated from general telemetry, and it is used only for the stated purpose.

**Why.** GDPR transparency and purpose limitation. AI Act Annex III(3)(b) if AI evaluates learning outcomes.

**How to improve.** Document what is assessed in the teacher guide and the child privacy notice; store assessment data separately.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj), [AIA-OMNIBUS](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes/)

### A-ECO-01: No paid randomised rewards (loot boxes)

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** No loot boxes, gacha, mystery chests or other variable rewards that can be obtained with money or with currency purchasable with money.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 13(2) bans variable reward systems on social and video services. DFA proposal bans paid loot boxes for minors in games.

**How to improve.** Replace with fixed, visible rewards earned through learning.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows)

### A-ECO-02: No pay-to-win

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: mixed · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Nothing bought with money gives a gameplay or learning advantage.

**Why.** DFA proposal bans pay-to-win for minors. Fairness in learning.

**How to improve.** Make all progression earnable through play; keep any paid items cosmetic and adult-purchased.

**Sources.** [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows), [UCPD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj)

### A-ECO-03: Virtual currency is not sold to children and shows its real value

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** In-game currency cannot be bought by a minor. If it can be bought by an adult, its value in euro is shown wherever it is spent, and it is off by default for children unless a guardian approves.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 13(1) (applied to chatbots via Art. 14(1)(c)). DFA proposal.

**How to improve.** Remove currency purchase from child screens; show euro equivalents; add guardian approval.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows), [UCPD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj)

### A-ECO-04: Rewards follow learning, not time or return visits

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Points, stars and unlocks are tied to learning progress or effort, not to time spent, number of sessions or returning at specific times.

**Why.** Aligning game mechanics with learning mechanics (LM-GM model) improves learning and avoids engagement-for-its-own-sake.

**How to improve.** Map each reward to a learning mechanic (Arnab et al. LM-GM) and remove rewards that only count time or logins.

**Sources.** [ARNAB2014](https://doi.org/10.1111/bjet.12113), [KIDS-COM](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026DC0680), [R-DECI1999](https://depts.washington.edu/techdocs/papers/deciExtrinsicRewardsAndIntrinsicMotivation99.pdf), [R-SAILER2020](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10648-019-09498-w), [R-HIRSHPASEK2015](https://www.psychologicalscience.org/publications/educational-apps.html)

### A-MOT-01: No reward pile-up

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: mixed · Effort: low

**Requirement.** The team keeps a reward inventory (points, coins, badges, streaks, levels, leaderboards, unlockables, celebrations) and records for each one whether it is given for learning or for showing up. No more than two layers are given for playing time, logging in or simply finishing.

**Why.** Expected rewards for doing a task lower later intrinsic motivation (d = -0.36), more in children. Badges plus leaderboards lowered motivation and exam scores over a semester. Each extra layer makes rewards more expected and more controlling. Stacking is an inference from single-element studies.

**How to improve.** Write the reward inventory (one line per layer, 'for learning' or 'for showing up'); remove or convert layers given for showing up.

**Sources.** [R-DECI1999](https://depts.washington.edu/techdocs/papers/deciExtrinsicRewardsAndIntrinsicMotivation99.pdf), [R-HANUS2015](https://www.smhp.psych.ucla.edu/pdfdocs/gamil.pdf), [R-MEKLER2017](https://glassmanlab.seas.harvard.edu/annotated_works/mekler17.pdf), [R-SAILER2020](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10648-019-09498-w), [R-RADESKY2022](https://www.michiganmedicine.org/health-lab/design-tricks-commonly-used-monetize-young-childrens-app-use)

### A-MOT-02: Feedback informs, it does not control

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: mixed · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Feedback says what the learner did well and why, and what to try next. Copy avoids controlling language ("you must", "you have to") and external goal framing ("do this to win coins").

**Why.** Informational verbal feedback raised intrinsic motivation (+0.33). Controlling language and external goal framing undermined conceptual learning in 11 to 12-year-olds, while drill scores looked fine, so the loss is easy to miss.

**How to improve.** Rewrite feedback strings as specific, informational messages; review copy for 'must' and reward-centred goals.

**Sources.** [R-DECI1999](https://depts.washington.edu/techdocs/papers/deciExtrinsicRewardsAndIntrinsicMotivation99.pdf), [R-VANSTEENKISTE2005](https://investigacion.pucp.edu.pe/grupos/motem/publicacion/examining-the-motivational-impact-of-intrinsic-vs-extrinsic-goal-framing-and-internally-controlling-vs-autonomy-supportive-communication-style-on-childrens-achievement/)

### A-MOT-03: The product works with rewards switched off

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** The teacher can switch off points, leaderboards and celebrations, or turn competition into a shared class or team goal, and the activity still makes sense. Teacher materials include debrief prompts that turn rewards into information ("What did you do to earn that?").

**Why.** Gamification's cognitive gains are robust, but motivational gains vanish in rigorous studies; competition combined with collaboration beats competition alone. Leaderboards reward those already ahead and hurt the weakest.

**How to improve.** Add teacher toggles for each reward layer and a 'team goal' mode; add debrief questions to the teacher guide.

**Sources.** [R-SAILER2020](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10648-019-09498-w), [R-HANUS2015](https://www.smhp.psych.ucla.edu/pdfdocs/gamil.pdf), [R-HIRSHPASEK2015](https://www.psychologicalscience.org/publications/educational-apps.html)

### A-MOT-04: Room for curiosity

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** The design includes open questions, things to explore, choices with consequences, and moments where learners explain their reasoning to each other. Success is not only a count of completed items.

**Why.** Curiosity improves memory through the same reward circuit that responds to coins, and predicts achievement, more strongly for children in poverty. Intrinsic motivation predicts quality of work and well-being; incentives predict quantity. Intrinsic motivation already declines through school.

**How to improve.** Add at least one exploratory or explain-your-reasoning moment per unit; track learning quality, not only items completed.

**Sources.** [R-GRUBER2014](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2014/10/141002123631.htm), [R-SHAH2018](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41390-018-0099-4), [R-CERASOLI2014](https://hillkm.com/EDUC_712/Cerasoli_Nicklin_Ford_2014.pdf), [R-HOWARD2021](https://acuresearchbank.acu.edu.au/item/8w8z7/student-motivation-and-associated-outcomes-a-meta-analysis-from-self-determination-theory), [R-LEPPER2005](https://www.reed.edu/psychology/motivation/assets/downloads/Lepper_Corpus_Iyengar_2005.pdf)

### A-MOT-05: Helping and creativity are recognised, not paid

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Helping others and cooperating are not paid with points or items. Creative tasks reward creative quality with informative feedback, not mere completion.

**Why.** Toddlers rewarded with a toy for helping later helped less. Rewards for completing creative tasks lower creativity; recognising creative quality with fair feedback can help.

**How to improve.** Replace point payouts for helping with acknowledgement; give creative tasks qualitative feedback instead of completion rewards.

**Sources.** [R-WARNEKEN2008](https://scholars.duke.edu/publication/1458228), [R-BYRON2012](https://www.frontiersin.org/article/10.3389/fpsyg.2020.00974)

### A-PLY-01: No penalties for not playing

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** No energy systems that only refill by waiting or paying, no pets or worlds that decay or die when the child is away, no loss of benefits for missing days.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(d) applied to online games by Art. 15(1)(a).

**How to improve.** Remove decay and energy timers; let the world wait for the child unchanged.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows), [R-RADESKY2022](https://www.michiganmedicine.org/health-lab/design-tricks-commonly-used-monetize-young-childrens-app-use)

### A-PLY-02: Non-shaming failure and feedback

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Errors and failures are presented as part of learning, without ridicule, sad animations directed at the child, or public exposure.

**Why.** Psychological safety supports learning, especially for younger children.

**How to improve.** Review all failure states with an instructional designer; use encouraging, specific feedback.

**Sources.** [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation), [ARNAB2014](https://doi.org/10.1111/bjet.12113)

### A-SOC-01: Multiplayer limited to closed groups

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: multiplayer · Detection: manual · Effort: high

**Requirement.** Multiplayer happens within teacher- or guardian-defined groups. Cross-group play only through adult-mediated pairing. The game cannot be used to lure children to other services.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 15(1)(c) and 15(2).

**How to improve.** Use class rooms with join codes controlled by the teacher; block sharing of external links and handles.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors)

### B-DAT-01: Research use of learning data is separated

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Learning data is only shared for research under a data sharing agreement, with legal basis, ethics approval and pseudonymisation, and never as a by-product of normal operation.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 5(1)(b), 6 and 89.

**How to improve.** Create a research export pipeline that pseudonymises and logs every extract.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### B-UGC-01: User-generated content is moderated and visible to the teacher

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: ugc, chat · Detection: mixed · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Content created or uploaded by children is moderated proportionally to age, visible to the responsible teacher, reportable, and not public. Uploaded media has metadata (e.g. GPS) stripped.

**Why.** DSA Art. 28 guidelines. KIDS Act Art. 12(3) and 19.

**How to improve.** Add teacher review queues, EXIF stripping on upload, and keep galleries class-private.

**Sources.** [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### B-UGC-02: No photos of children's faces kept or shared beyond need

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: ugc · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Photos and videos of children are only stored when necessary for the learning activity, are never public, expire automatically, and others cannot download them.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 12(3)(e). GDPR minimisation and storage limitation.

**How to improve.** Prefer avatars; add auto-expiry and disable download of child media.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### C-ENG-01: Streaks are optional and never punish

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: streaks · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Streaks can be switched off, carry no loss framing, and missing a day costs nothing (free freezes or no reset).

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(d) (penalties for not engaging). DFA proposal: right to switch off streak rewards.

**How to improve.** Add a 'turn off streaks' setting and replace 'you will lose your streak' with neutral progress messages.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows)

### C-ENG-02: Leaderboards are class-scoped and pseudonymous

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: leaderboards · Detection: static · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Leaderboards are limited to the class or group, show avatars or nicknames, can be disabled by the teacher, and never publicly rank named children.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 11(3) (social comparison). GDPR minimisation.

**How to improve.** Scope leaderboards to class, use nicknames, add a teacher toggle, and consider showing personal bests only.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [R-HANUS2015](https://www.smhp.psych.ucla.edu/pdfdocs/gamil.pdf), [R-SAILER2020](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10648-019-09498-w)

### C-ENG-04: No variable reward schedules designed for engagement

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Rewards are predictable and earned. Random bonus drops and slot-machine style surprises are avoided.

**Why.** Variable ratio rewards drive compulsive use. KIDS Act Art. 13(2) bans them in spending contexts on social and video services.

**How to improve.** Replace random bonuses with predictable milestones the child can see in advance.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [KIDS-COM](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026DC0680), [R-DECI1999](https://depts.washington.edu/techdocs/papers/deciExtrinsicRewardsAndIntrinsicMotivation99.pdf), [R-DIXON2013](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2013/07/130702100348.htm)

### C-ENG-05: Engagement metrics balanced by wellbeing metrics

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Product KPIs for minors include learning and wellbeing outcomes, not only time spent, sessions or retention.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 10(2) asks recommender optimisation to include quality and mental health metrics; good practice for every product.

**How to improve.** Add learning-gain and healthy-session-length metrics to the product dashboard and goals.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [KIDS-COM](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026DC0680), [EUKO](https://www.lse.ac.uk/media-and-communications/research/research-projects/eu-kids-online), [R-CERASOLI2014](https://hillkm.com/EDUC_712/Cerasoli_Nicklin_Ford_2014.pdf)

### C-ENG-06: Challenges without anxiety timers for younger children

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: B1 (3-5), B2 (6-9), B3 (10-12) · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Quests and challenges for under-13s avoid countdown timers and expiring rewards.

**Why.** Time pressure creates anxiety and drives compulsive return.

**How to improve.** Remove expiry from quests or extend them to the whole school term.

**Sources.** [KIDS-COM](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026DC0680), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation)
